## Themes

These rows serve two aims. A worker's brief reaches it intact and running workers can be told apart (two adopts into `delegation`). Git safety stays enforced: our guard hook already holds most of the upstream rules, and the one place it falls short, git options before the subcommand, is closed by a fix of the hook itself, which is not a registry unit. The rest is rejected: co-writing with a person, conversation handoff, commit-time checks and TypeScript test data have no place among ours, and the course scaffold is out of scope.

11. candidate-openings-distinct-theses: Draft two or three openings each implying a different thesis, show all, and make the user pick or build a hybrid (SKILL.md:23).
12. opening-defines-obligations: The chosen opening sets what the rest of the article must deliver (SKILL.md:23).
13. reader-needs-next-question: Grow the article by asking what the reader must hear next given what is written (SKILL.md:24).
14. deliberate-block-format: Argue the form of each block (paragraph, list, table, callout, quote, code) so each choice is defensible (SKILL.md:24).
15. append-each-agreed-block: Write each agreed block to the file immediately, not in batches (SKILL.md:25, 71).
16. user-decides-done: The user, not the agent, says when the article is finished (SKILL.md:26).
17. adversarial-editor-stance: Push back, refuse weak transitions, and cut paragraphs that do not earn their place (SKILL.md:43).
18. standing-challenge-questions: Keep asking what each paragraph adds, what breaks if cut, prose versus list, split double-duty sentences, and whether the article drifted from its opening's promise (SKILL.md:45-51).
19. pile-as-quarry-one-voice: Rework, split, merge or paraphrase pile material so the article reads as one voice (SKILL.md:55).
20. name-material-gaps: When the pile lacks something needed, say so and ask the user to supply it now or cut the section (SKILL.md:57).
21. prose-vs-list-rule: Use prose for argument and lists only for truly parallel items (SKILL.md:63).
22. callout-only-if-derailing: Put tips and warnings in callouts only when inline they would derail the argument (SKILL.md:64).
23. table-at-three-repeats: Use a table when the same field shape repeats three or more times, otherwise prose with bold leads (SKILL.md:65).
24. quote-when-wording-matters: Quote when exact wording is the point, paraphrase otherwise (SKILL.md:66).
25. code-block-vs-inline-rule: Multi-line, runnable or illustrative code goes in a block; single tokens inline (SKILL.md:67).
26. format-tradeoffs-out-loud: Discuss format tradeoffs with the user rather than deciding silently (SKILL.md:61).
27. reread-before-every-write: Re-read the article before every write and never overwrite blindly (SKILL.md:71).
28. targeted-paragraph-rewrite: Rewrite only the requested paragraph in place (SKILL.md:71).
29. no-new-material-mining: Gathering new fragments outside the pile is out of scope; gaps are named instead (SKILL.md:75).
30. no-publishing-or-unrequested-frontmatter: Platform formatting, publishing and unrequested frontmatter are out of scope (SKILL.md:77).

## skill:skills/misc/git-guardrails-claude-code

Compared with `none`; upstream tree hash `7aa92e9d469c6cd0b24ed8accb2e4be681c44c1524d71604c06b4055b7b56482`.

| Holder | Overlap | Placement match |
|---|---|---|
| doc:.repo-context/verification.md | 1 |  |

Suggested: none · purpose match: none · flag: none
Purpose: Upstream installs a hook that blocks dangerous git commands. Ours already ships such a hook as project configuration; a hook is not a skill and cannot be compared.
Reason: Compared with none: our equivalent is a hook, outside the registry's skill comparison.

### Blind extraction

1. pre-tool-command-hook: Install a hook that inspects shell commands before execution and blocks dangerous git ones (SKILL.md:8).
2. blocked-command-list: The blocked set is pushes of any kind, hard resets, forced cleans, forced branch deletion, and whole-tree checkout or restore (SKILL.md:10-16).
3. no-authority-message: A blocked agent is told it lacks authority to run that command (SKILL.md:18).
4. ask-install-scope: Ask whether to install for this project or for all projects (SKILL.md:22-24).
5. copy-script-by-scope: Copy the bundled script into a project or user hooks folder per the chosen scope (SKILL.md:26-33).
6. make-script-executable: Mark the copied script executable (SKILL.md:35).
7. settings-hook-registration-template: Register the script as a command hook on the shell tool in the matching settings file, using a project-dir variable for project scope and a home path for global (SKILL.md:37-79).
8. merge-not-overwrite-settings: Merge into an existing hook array without disturbing other settings (SKILL.md:81).
9. offer-pattern-customization: Ask whether to add or remove blocked patterns, and edit the copied script accordingly (SKILL.md:83-85).
10. pipe-test-verification: Verify by piping a sample push command as hook input and expecting exit code 2 with a blocked message on stderr (SKILL.md:87-95).
11. reads-hook-json-from-stdin: Reads the hook payload from standard input and extracts the command field with a JSON tool, which is therefore required (block-dangerous-git.sh:3-4).
12. regex-pattern-blocklist: Holds nine extended-regex patterns: push, hard reset, forced clean (two forms), forced branch delete, checkout-dot, restore-dot, plus bare "push --force" and "reset --hard" fragments that also catch git invocations with options before the subcommand (block-dangerous-git.sh:6-16).
13. substring-match-anywhere: A pattern matching anywhere in the command string blocks it, so the pattern inside a longer command or quoted text also triggers (block-dangerous-git.sh:18-19).
14. block-with-exit-2-and-stderr-reason: On a match, prints to stderr a message naming the command and the matched pattern and saying the user prevented it, then exits 2 (block-dangerous-git.sh:20-21).
15. first-match-stops: Stops checking at the first matching pattern (block-dangerous-git.sh:18-23).
16. allow-by-default: Any command matching no pattern exits 0 and is allowed (block-dangerous-git.sh:25).

### Mapping

- 1 → pre-run-git-command-guard (new)
- 2 → block-every-push, pre-run-git-command-guard (split)
- 3 → refusal-without-recourse (new)
- 4 → guard-install-scope-choice (new)
- 5 → guard-hook-install (new)
- 6 → guard-hook-install (new)
- 7 → guard-hook-install (new)
- 8 → settings-merge-not-overwrite (new)
- 9 → guard-pattern-customization (new)
- 10 → guard-hook-block-proof (match)
- 11 → hook-payload-needs-json-tool (new)
- 12 → bare-force-push-reset-fragments (new)
- 13 → match-anywhere-in-command (new)
- 14 → first-match-block-else-allow (new)
- 15 → first-match-block-else-allow (new)
- 16 → first-match-block-else-allow (new)

### Traits

- `pre-run-git-command-guard` (new): absent; reject; reason: Already in force here: `.claude/hooks/block-dangerous-commands.sh` blocks each of these before a shell command runs, registered at `.claude/settings.json:3-12`, and the plugin's template carries the same registration to every repository it sets up. A hook is not a unit the registry compares, so no row can show it as held; a second hook would duplicate it.
- `block-every-push` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours blocks only forced pushes (`.claude/hooks/block-dangerous-commands.sh`:20-21) and lets an authorized push run, as `AGENTS.md:72` allows; blocking every push would stop pushes the owner asked for.
- `refusal-without-recourse` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours tells the agent to ask the user before proceeding (`.claude/hooks/block-dangerous-commands.sh`:33), because AGENTS.md allows these commands with explicit approval (`AGENTS.md:70-73`); a flat refusal would leave a sanctioned request with no path.
- `guard-install-scope-choice` (new): absent; reject; reason: Our guard ships as project configuration with the harness, so a repository gets it by adopting the harness; a user-wide install would act in repositories that never chose it.
- `guard-hook-install` (new): absent; reject; reason: Nothing to install: `.claude/hooks/block-dangerous-commands.sh` and its registration already ship with the harness (`.claude/settings.json:3-12`).
- `settings-merge-not-overwrite` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: A unit of ours comes to edit a harness settings file in a repository by hand.; reason: Sound, but no unit of ours writes into a settings file by hand now, so there is no place it would change what an agent does.
- `guard-pattern-customization` (new): absent; reject; reason: A pattern changes through an ordinary reviewed edit to `.claude/hooks/block-dangerous-commands.sh`, proven with a forbidden payload as `.repo-context/verification.md:37-41` requires; an install-time prompt adds no safety.
- `guard-hook-block-proof` (new): absent; reject; also in doc:.repo-context/verification.md (present); reason: Held whole by `.repo-context/verification.md:37-41`, which round 2026-10-14-migration took from this skill; that file is not the compared skill or AGENTS.md, so the row cannot show it as held, and a second copy would add nothing.
- `hook-payload-needs-json-tool` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours reads it with a JSON tool when one is installed and falls back to plain text matching when not (`.claude/hooks/block-dangerous-commands.sh`:10-14); requiring the tool would make the hook error out where it is missing, and an erroring hook lets the command run.
- `bare-force-push-reset-fragments` (new): absent; reject; reason: Held by the guard hook once bead cr-oez0's fix lands (owner ruling 2026-11-13); the hook is not a registry unit.
- `match-anywhere-in-command` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours already matches anywhere in the command (`.claude/hooks/block-dangerous-commands.sh`:31-32), choosing to over-block rather than miss a real one; that also blocks some harmless commands, such as checking out a file whose name starts with a dot, which the owner can weigh with the gap above.
- `first-match-block-else-allow` (new): absent; reject; reason: Held whole by ours: it exits 2 on the first match with a message naming the command and the pattern, and exits 0 otherwise (`.claude/hooks/block-dangerous-commands.sh`:31-35, :89); a hook is not a unit the registry compares, so the row cannot show it as held.

- `lockfile-package-manager` (new): absent; reject; reason: Specific to JavaScript package managers, which owner ruling E of 2026-11-05 keeps rejected with Husky; a stack-neutral version would take its commands from the repository's own `.repo-context/verification.md`.
